hero.statusText: Bujumbura, Burundi — a sanctuary for survivors is being built
hero.text1: In Burundi, more than one woman in five has survived violence from an intimate partner. Iwacu Collective Center is being built for them — and for the children who need a safe place to grow.
hero.text2: A sanctuary of resilience where every survivor transforms trauma into the strength to take full control of their life again.

mission.imagePlaceholder: Portrait of a mother and child, direct and warm, natural light.
mission.heading: A sanctuary of resilience, in the making.
mission.paragraph1: Iwacu means "our home" in Kirundi. Iwacu Collective Center (ICC) is being created in Burundi as an integrated center of care for survivors of gender-based violence and extremely vulnerable children.
mission.paragraph2: Our mission is to build a future without violence: accompanying survivors and vulnerable children toward lasting independence through holistic care and productive projects, and acting on the roots of injustice by promoting positive masculinity and changed behavior.
mission.quote: "Restore hope, rebuild lives, transform the future." — Our vision

work.heading: Nine pillars.
work.desc1: A first welcome by a social worker, psychosocial and psychological support, medical referral, legal and judicial assistance — and childcare services for the most vulnerable.
work.desc2: Agro-pastoral and entrepreneurial training, income-generating activities and cash transfers for lasting financial independence — plus family reintegration and referral pathways for orphans and vulnerable children.
work.desc3: Engaging men and boys as champions of positive masculinity, transforming the social norms that allow violence to persist, and integrating research into everything we do.

about.heroDescription: Iwacu Collective Center is being built in Burundi as an integrated center for survivors of gender-based violence and extremely vulnerable children. This is who we are, why we started, and where we are going.
about.portraitPlaceholder: Wide view of the future site of Iwacu Collective Center in Burundi
about.portraitCaptionLeft: The future home of Iwacu Collective Center · Burundi
about.storySidebarHeading: Why Iwacu exists — and where we're going.
about.storyP1: Iwacu was born from a dream carried for more than twenty years. After two decades working in programs against gender inequality and social injustice — listening every day to women and girls surviving violence of every kind, and the inhuman treatment they endure — our founder made a promise: to create a place where survivors and the most vulnerable children are welcomed, healed, and free to rebuild their lives.
about.storyP2: Today that dream is becoming real. Iwacu Collective Center is being created in Burundi, bringing together the experience of a lifetime and strategic alliances with other actors — contributing to the national priorities of the PND and Vision 2040–2060.
about.beliefP1: Our goal is not to create dependence, but to restore the power to act. We exist to offer survivors the care and training to take their destiny into their own hands — and to give orphaned and vulnerable children the quality education they need to become the authors of their own future.
about.beliefP2: That belief shapes every pillar of the center: holistic healing, medical and legal care, agro-pastoral and entrepreneurial training, and the engagement of men and boys as allies. Because a community is only truly safe when everyone helps protect it.
about.blockquote: "Restore hope, rebuild lives, transform the future."
about.blockquoteCite: — The vision of Iwacu Collective Center
about.notDoP1: A welcome without judgment. Absolute confidentiality — strict protection of personal data and total professional ethics in every medical, legal and psychosocial accompaniment. Empathy and warmth, because healing depends on it. And empowerment always: we walk beside survivors until they no longer need us.
about.notDoP2: These commitments are not slogans. They are the conditions of trust — and for survivors whose trust has been broken, they are everything.
about.valuesDescription: These are the values written into the founding vision of Iwacu Collective Center — the rules we will carry into every program, every partnership, and every welcome.
about.val1Text: Every person — whatever their past, whatever their status — is treated with absolute consideration. A welcome without judgment; the self-esteem of every participant protected.
about.val2Text: For survivors of violence, trust is often broken. We must be irreproachable: strict management of personal data, and total professional ethics in legal, medical and psychosocial care.
about.val3Text: Understanding another's suffering in order to help them better. Active listening and a warm environment — essential to the development of children and to the healing of survivors.
about.val4Text: Not dependence — the power to act. Training so survivors take their destiny into their own hands, and a quality education so orphans become the authors of their own future.
about.val5Text: Working together to break the cycle of violence and poverty — with communities, host families, partners and public services, building a safety net around the most vulnerable.
about.teamDescription: Our team is taking shape. The women and men who will lead the center will be introduced here.
about.contactDescription: Whether you're considering a partnership, a story, a visit, or a gift — we'd like to hear from you.
